Grief & loss

Grief, Loss & Bereavement

Grief is a natural response to loss. It may follow a death, relationship change, illness, infertility, job loss, major transition, or another meaningful change.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

There is no single correct way to grieve

Grief can involve sadness, anger, guilt, relief, numbness, yearning, difficulty concentrating, sleep changes, or periods of feeling relatively normal. It rarely follows a predictable sequence.

How counseling can help

Grief counseling can provide space to process the loss, adjust to changes in identity or routine, work through guilt or unfinished feelings, communicate with family, and rebuild meaningful activities without suggesting that the loss should simply be “gotten over.”

When additional evaluation may help

Seek professional support when grief remains intensely disabling, safety becomes a concern, substance use escalates, or symptoms of depression, trauma, or anxiety become difficult to manage.

Use the counselor directory to compare providers by specialty, approach, location, insurance, availability, and visit type.
